summary: This Restaurant class holds one method that turns a numeric spice level (1 through 5) into a readable description like "Mild" or "Spicy". It is written as a small, easily testable unit: give it a number, get a string back.

lines.text: The class is a container for restaurant behaviour; right now it only knows how to describe spice levels, and later exercises add more methods to it.
The method takes the level as an int and hands back a String, so a test can compare the returned text to an expected value without any printing or user interaction.
This is a switch expression: the whole switch produces a single value that is returned immediately, rather than assigning to a variable in each branch.
The arrow form matches level 1 and yields its description with no break statement needed, so there is no risk of accidentally falling through to the next case.
Level 5 is the top of the documented range, which makes it a natural boundary value to cover in a unit test.
Any number outside 1 through 5 lands here, which both satisfies the compiler's demand that a switch expression always produce a value and gives tests a defined result for bad input such as 0 or 6.
